versions.localizedDescription: # Theft4 0.3.1 — Performance Improvements **iPhone and iPad · version 0.3.1 · build 142** A performance follow-up to the direct Metal release: less repeated CPU work, cheaper first-use geometry, fewer allocations and better cache behavior. The original Theft4 icon is back. ## What changed - Faster cold geometry conversion and reusable immutable upload backing. - Less work per draw through cached shader metadata, pooled bindings and reusable frame bookkeeping. - Warm pipeline recipes survive cache pressure instead of being cleared together. - Upload VM allocation runs outside the cache mutex; retired sources are cleaned up incrementally and in-flight GPU resources retain their data. - Less CPU busy polling and allocation in multi-object waits. - Native attachment optimizations reduce proven redundant clear/load/store work while preserving the intended image. - Improved compact iPhone launcher layouts. ## Optional Mods menu - **Native Aspect Ratio:** expand the viewport to the launch-window shape, with matching camera/lighting reconstruction, odd-size effects fixes and proportional pause-menu/radar corrections. More visible scenery can increase frame time. - **Custom Time Cycle:** lighting/weather replacement for loose and packed installs. **Credit and thanks to SBerrix** for the custom time cycle. - **God Mode:** player damage/death protection. - **Unlimited Ammo:** reserve ammunition stays available while magazines deplete and reload normally. Select mods before Play; changes take effect on a fresh game launch. The realistic vehicle-handling mod remains planned work and is not included. ## Older devices GPUs without BC-texture support retain the one-time BC-to-ASTC preparation flow: progress, ETA, pause/resume and a saved cache reused on later launches. The tested A12Z uses it; the tested M5 supports BC directly and skips it. The check uses GPU capability rather than an age cutoff. Updating in place retains existing caches. ## Validation and current limits 33 native contracts, 9 mod contracts and 45 real-Metal graphics cases pass, alongside CPU wait sanitizer checks and Release optimization verification. The target remains under 30 ms of total frame work. Remaining first-use spikes, heavy views and device-specific performance are still being improved; this is not a universal locked-30-FPS guarantee. Host fixture savings are not whole-game FPS percentages. Optional mod coverage still needs broader gameplay testing. [Full changelog](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/CHANGELOG.md) · [0.3.1 release details](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/docs/RELEASE_0.3.1.md) · [Technical changes and evidence](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3.1/docs/IOS_MODS.md) ## Install the IPA 1. Download **Theft4-0.3.1-142-ios-arm64.ipa** below. The Source code ZIP is not the IPA. 2. Install with a compatible sideloading tool such as AltStore or SideStore. The IPA is unsigned; your tool must sign it with your Apple account. **Update the existing app in place** to retain game files, saves and prepared textures. Do not delete the app first. 3. For a new install, launch once to create **Files → On My iPhone/iPad → Theft4 → game**, then close the app. 4. Prepare your legally obtained supported Xbox 360 USA retail game: title `545407F2`, media `6AC07221`, base `0.0.0.5`, matching TU8 patch to `0.0.8.5`. A raw ISO or unopened update package is not a prepared installation. 5. Copy the prepared folder's contents into Theft4's existing `game` folder. `default.xex` and `default.xexp` must be at its root, not under `game/game`. 6. Reopen, **Check Game Files**, complete ASTC preparation if required, then Play. Requires ARM64 iOS/iPadOS 26.0 or later. No retail game installation, title update, save, prepared texture cache or developer provisioning profile is included. The credited custom time-cycle resources are included. TestFlight is separate. [Complete installation instructions](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft

# Theft4 0.3 — direct Metal and a rebuilt rendering path Apple version **0.3.0**, build **123**, launcher label **0.3**. Source and the full engineering record are published on GitHub main. The [0.3 GitHub release](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/releases/tag/v0.3) includes the unsigned ARM64 IPA and its checksum. TestFlight publication is separate. The full engineering changelog is [recorded here](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3/CHANGELOG.md#03--direct-metal-rebuilt-geometry-and-a-faster-native-rendering-path--2026-10-06). 0.3 is the largest rendering change in Theft4 so far. The running game now sends its prepared frames directly to Metal. This includes the actual city, characters, lighting, effects and presentation, rather than just the separate Metal Lab. The renderer and its CPU preparation, resource lifetimes and upload caches have been substantially rebuilt around Apple's graphics API. On the M5 iPad, the tester reports a huge improvement and very good gameplay at the selected native resolution, with a remaining spike that now recovers. Subsequent build 122 testing was also reported as excellent. The latest retrieved native log confirms a 2416×1359 internal/output target with no upscaling. This is much closer to the desired console experience. It does not establish a locked 30 FPS in every scene, uninterrupted long-session stability, or equivalent performance on other hardware. The engineering target remains under 30 ms of frame work, leaving margin inside the 33.3 ms interval for 30 FPS. ## The direct Metal change The previous production rendering route used the GTA IV frontend, Vulkan and MoltenVK before reaching Metal. 0.3 introduces a live Metal worker, native render passes, native resource bindings, completion-owned frame storage and direct CAMetalLayer presentation. Normal Metal gameplay does not realize its draws through the Vulkan provider or presenter. Game shaders are prepared offline from the project's stock shader corpus. Their constant banks and reflected texture/sampler fetches become explicit Metal bindings. The game no longer needs to compile that corpus through a live Vulkan translation path to produce its Metal draws. Pipeline variants and Metal driver compilation can still require work when a new scene is encountered. The game remains an ahead-of-time recompilation of the supported Xbox 360 release. Its compiled ARM64 code still uses the compatibility runtime for the title's memory, service and calling conventions. This release does not replace all game logic with handwritten native code, rewrite physics or traffic, or turn the project into a PC source port. Legacy Vulkan code and libraries remain in the build for comparison and compatibility; direct rendering is a runtime route, not a claim that the application has no Vulkan symbols or dependencies. ## Rendering correctness and clarity - Complete ordered frames now include the game's render passes, color resolves, depth handoffs, reflections and host effects. Draw order and required prior attachment contents are preserved across internal submissions. - The port handles reversed viewport depth, the negative-one-to-one vertex depth convention, attachmentless draws, depth-only pipelines, per-instance stream 16, buffered/indexed rectangles and rotating output drawables. - Packed lighting aliases and the title's float-pair multiple render targets retain their intended channel masks and storage roles. GPU-produced surfaces are distinct from immutable uploaded textures. - Sampling preserves mip ranges, row/plane pitches, layers, cube faces and channel swizzles. Reflection updates wait for valid written content rather than making an entire otherwise valid scene fail. - Blending, alpha discard, sample coverage, output scaling and clamping are checked against the game shader contract. Normal presentation uses GPU textures directly. - Color targets use render-appropriate private storage without unnecessary usage flags that defeated compr

# Theft4 0.2.1 — important iOS update Version 0.2.1 (build 53) is an important update for iPhone and iPad. It keeps the official `com.lukebrosious.theft4` app identity, so an in-place update preserves the existing app container, game installation, settings, caches, and saves. Do not delete the old app before updating. The GitHub `ios-arm64.ipa` is unsigned and must be signed by the user's sideloading tool. The TestFlight build is separately signed by Apple. Neither artifact contains copyrighted game files, title updates, user saves, signing identities, or provisioning profiles. Public sideload artifact: `Theft4-0.2.1-53-ios-arm64.ipa` SHA-256: `3f278f0d3b07cfdda0e40a3672594d17bcd0499c01484d86b0a1845b7f571f9a` ## User-facing changes - New After Hours launcher presentation and updated Theft4 app icon. - Gameplay uses the proven centered 16:9 presentation on iPhone and iPad. The initial build 52 device-aspect experiment was withdrawn after testing exposed stretched world geometry, misaligned shadows, incomplete HUD correction, and increased frame-time instability. It will return only after the world, shadow, post-process and HUD projections are validated together. - New **Auto Optimize for This Device** and **Original Xbox 360 Settings** buttons. Both are explicit, reversible starting points; manual changes still persist. - Graphics choices include Native Pixels, 540p, 720p, 900p, and 1080p scene resolution, with FSR controlled independently where supported. Native Pixels uses the largest centered 16:9 physical-pixel target that fits the display. - Expanded controls for shadows, draw distance, model detail, reflections, edge smoothing, anisotropic filtering, motion blur, and depth of field. - New save export/import in **System**. Import validates the selected export and creates a dated backup of the current saves before replacement. - Improved touch-control, frame-counter, frame-time graph, diagnostic status, and Files export behavior. - iOS Game Mode metadata is declared for the official app. ## Limited-memory device protection iPhones and iPads with less than 7 GiB of usable memory are treated as limited-memory devices. This covers the 6 GB class and older/lower-memory models without changing the defaults on devices with 8 GB or more. On a limited-memory device, settings that would create unnecessary rendering or memory pressure are constrained at launch and whenever graphics settings are changed: - 1080p and Native requests are capped at 900p with FSR and fixed 1080p output; - existing lower 540p and 720p selections remain lower rather than being raised; - original shadow size, optimized draw distance, original model detail and reflections are used; - additional edge smoothing, anisotropic filtering, motion blur, depth of field, and the optional FSR sharpening boost are disabled; - launcher choices above the supported ceiling are visibly unavailable. This is a pressure-control policy, not proof that resolution caused every reported failure. In particular, tester logs associated guest texture handle `D8FFC2B0` with an image-creation failure on 6 GB iPhones, but the handle alone does not identify the allocation root cause. The cap is a safe mitigation while the new capture evidence is used to separate memory, pipeline, CPU, and GPU causes. Newer 8 GB-and-up devices keep their existing device-optimized choices. ## Performance and renderer work - Reduced producer/worker command-transfer copying, allocation, and lock hold time with batched transfer and bounded storage reuse. - Avoided redundant resource-binding notifications and repeated vertex/index binding when validated state is unchanged. - Reused immutable vertex-layout requirements and validated shader-constant parent snapshots; changed constant ranges are projected into fenced frame allocations instead of rematerializing whole blocks. - Improved persistent-buffer reuse accounting, resource retirement, descriptor handling, pipeline diagnostics, resolve synchronization, and fr

M5 Lab 0.1.3 (41) is now the foundation of the official Theft4 app. This 0.2.0b release adds first-launch game setup and System → Download Latest Log Capture to that Lab renderer and launcher. Highlights: batched render-command delivery, reduced redundant state work, bounded pipeline preparation and frame resources, independent internal resolution and FSR controls, performance preset, FPS/frame-time display, and bounded 600-frame diagnostics. The capture can be exported after quitting and reopening the app. Apple version: 0.2.0 (44). Bundle ID: com.lukebrosious.theft4. The historical com.theft4.m5lab app has a separate data container; copy or back up game files and saves before removing it. This IPA is unsigned for sideload tools to re-sign. No game data is included. Measured Lab command-delivery improvements are detailed in the README. They are directional captures, not a claim of locked 30 FPS or measured heat reduction. # Air 6.0.0 正式版 —— 渲染体系重构 + 装机反馈集中根治 5.1.0 之后累计 **60+ 次提交**，聚焦渲染体系（每游戏渲染器 + mg 全后端 FSR）与装机反馈问题根治。本版为第二个正式发行版。 ## ✨ 重点功能 - **渲染器每游戏强制单选**：设置页的全局渲染器选择退役，每个游戏在自己的设置页单独选择渲染器，未单独设置过的实例缺省"自动"（1.17+ 自动解析为 Vulkan 直连）。MobileGL 家族在渲染器列表里合并为唯一的 **mg** 条目：后端统一在 设置 > MobileGlues > 渲染后端 选择（Vulkan 直连 / GLES / OpenGL 4.0，默认 Vulkan 直连）。 - **mg 三个后端全部支持 FSR 1.0 超分**：GLES / OpenGL 4.0 后端为原生 EASU 放大 + RCAS 锐化双管线；**Vulkan 直连后端通过 Metal 呈现层拦截方案支持 FSR**（私有低分辨率交换层 + AMD FSR1 EASU/RCAS 移植到 Metal，MobileGL/MoltenVK 二进制零改动）——选择 FSR 档位即享受"低分辨率渲染 + 放大锐化"的帧率红利，Vulkan 直连推荐作为默认首选后端。 - **ES / OpenGL 4.0 黑屏根治**：强制开启的 DSA 扩展在 MobileGlues 模拟层 + FSR1 fb0 重定向下产生黑屏（多轮装机 A/B 实锤），已改回默认关闭并自动迁移存量配置。 - **新拟态 UI + 自定义背景**、**公告置顶**（推荐服务器 mysv.dpdns.org 已置顶）、**管理 Java 26.0+（Java 25）预选**、**TouchController 虚拟按钮回归**、**下载镜像策略**（默认加载速度快优先）等，完整清单见 README。 ## 🔧 装机反馈集中修复（Task 165-169） - CurseForge 加载源"无法使用"根治：镜像网关错误（上游瞬态 403/500 被包成无 data 键的 HTTP 200 JSON）不再被静默当成"无结果"——自动重试一次并把真实错误显示出来 - 本地整合包从"文件"App / 下载 / iCloud **任意位置选择即可直接安装**（不再需要先导入到应用文件） - 主页头像 **10s 超时 + 磁盘缓存秒显**（不再"要点一下才有"） - JIT 等待 **120s 超时 + 重试弹窗**（开启 JIT 偶发失败不再无限卡在"正在开启 JIT"） - Vulkan 直连首帧崩溃（交换链几何）、ES/4.0 函数解析层（gl* 符号劫持）等渲染链修复 ## 📦 安装 - 普通侧载（AltStore/SideStore/爱思助手等）：`AngelAuraAmethyst-6.0.0.ipa` - TrollStore：`AngelAuraAmethyst-6.0.0.tipa` - 首次启动游戏需要开启 JIT（设置 > JIT 里可选择 StikDebug / SideStore / JITStreamer 等工具） ## 🙏 反馈 遇到问题请上传 `latestlog.txt`（设置 > 日志）到仓库 Issues，带日志的问题基本都能一轮定位。 --- **Full changelog**: https://github.com/Gsjsjzhznsz/Air-Minecraft-iOS-Launcher/commits/main

versions.localizedDescription: # Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3. ## Put any button anywhere Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under **Button Mapping**. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update. The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that. ## Three bugs that were costing you frames **Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game.** One setting's name was a prefix of another's (`..._fps_cap` inside `..._fps_cap_auto`), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat. **"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion."** Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now. Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel. **A profiler was running in every build.** A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it. ## First launch could come up blank Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready. ## New in Settings Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone: - **3D Scene Resolution** — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness - **Draw Distance** — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth - **NPC Update Rate** and **World Update Rate** - **Pedestrians & Traffic**, **Movable Props**, **Other Skaters** — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart) - **Vegetation**, **Hair Detail**, **Water Effects**, **Draw Batching** - **Framerate Cap** — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz) - **FPS Percentiles** — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit). Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same. ## Two changed defaults on iOS - **Draw distance now ships at Half.** The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. The trade is real: props, street furniture and foliage pop in closer than they did in 2.6.3. **Settings > Video > Draw Distance > Original** puts it back. **This applies to new installs only.** If you are updating, your existing draw distance is kept exactly as it is — the

> **Superseded by [v2.7.1](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** > This build shipped the in-app title-update install, which still works exactly as described below. > It also shipped the Framerate Cap row that silently erased the 60 fps cap on every later launch — fixed in 2.7.1. ### Original v2.6.3 notes **The title update can now be installed from inside the app.** Previously iOS could do neither half of this: the "select a file" route went through the system document picker, which does not work under TrollStore or on a jailbreak, and the download button was never shown at all. Players who had just installed from a disc image were left able to install the game and then unable to install the update it requires. Both routes work now: - **Download it in the app.** Tap "Install the title update" and then Download. It fetches the 1.7 MB package and installs it, with no computer involved. - **Or copy it in yourself.** A package already sitting in your Skate 3 folder is found automatically, the same way disc images have been found since 2.6.0. No picker, no file browser. **A home screen on iOS.** The app now opens on a launcher instead of straight into the game: Play, install from a disc image, install the title update, choose a map pack, and save a diagnostic report you can share from the Files app. Every row returns to it, so you can install a disc, then the update, then pick a pack in one sitting. **Settings now stick.** Twenty-four rows were being forced back to their defaults at every launch - resolution, V-Sync, MSAA, shadows, ambient occlusion, bloom, sun shafts, draw distance, the frame cap, and the audio and interface rows. The menu wrote your choice to disk and startup overwrote it on the way back in, so the rows looked broken. Audio Buffer Size in particular simply never applied. Opening and closing the settings menu also used to freeze the per-device memory budgets at whatever that one launch happened to pick; it no longer writes rows you did not touch. **Map pack names in other languages.** A pack built for one market carries English text and leaves the other languages empty, and the game was showing those empty slots - an unnamed entry in the map list and raw identifiers where level names belong, reported as the DLC maps not loading in French or Spanish. Names now fall back to English instead of coming back blank. This is fixed in the game rather than in the packs, so it applies to every pack you already have. Requires iOS 16.0 or later and a 6-core device. You still supply your own copy of the game.

# Playport 0.3.3: JIT your way **Playport now works with the JIT tools you already use.** Its built-in JIT helper is still the easiest way to play. But if you already enable JIT with **StikDebug**, or run your apps inside **LiveContainer**, Playport now takes JIT from them too. You no longer need Playport's own pairing. ## Highlights ### 🔌 Choose where JIT comes from A new **JIT method** setting in **Settings › Setup check** (or press **X** on the setup checklist's first step) offers three ways: | Method | What happens when you press Play | | --- | --- | | **Built-in** (default) | Playport's own helper enables JIT, as before. No other app, no app switch. | | **StikDebug** | Playport opens StikDebug, which enables JIT and brings you back to the game. | | **Another app** | Playport waits for JIT from the app you use, such as LiveContainer's *Launch with JIT*. | StikDebug and other apps use StikDebug's standard **`universal.js`** script. Playport's JIT already speaks its protocol, so there is no custom script to install. ### 📦 LiveContainer support LiveContainer can't start Playport's built-in helper, so Playport now notices when it runs inside LiveContainer and hides the Built-in method. Two ways to play: 1. **Launch with JIT** (recommended): in LiveContainer, set the JIT enabler to StikDebug with `universal.js`, and turn on *Launch with JIT* for Playport. Playport finds JIT already there, so Play doesn't wait for it. 2. **StikDebug from Playport**: choose StikDebug as the JIT method and turn on *Use LiveContainer's Bundle ID* in LiveContainer's settings. ### 🧭 A setup that fits your method - With StikDebug or another app, Playport's own **pairing is no longer a setup step**, and a missing pairing never stops a game. - LocalDevVPN is skipped too when another app brings JIT. StikDebug still uses it. - While a game waits for JIT, the launch screen says what it is waiting for. If JIT doesn't arrive, it tells you what to check for the method you chose. ## Good to know - **One game per launch.** After a game, Playport normally restarts itself so the next one gets fresh JIT. That restart needs Playport's pairing, and inside LiveContainer it isn't possible at all. In those cases Playport asks you to close it and launch it again (with JIT) before the next game. - **Built-in is unchanged** and still the default. If it works for you, there is nothing to do. - **Not tested with StikDebug or LiveContainer yet.** Playport is tested on one phone (iOS 27.0), which has neither. Built-in was checked with Hollow Knight. If you play through StikDebug or LiveContainer, please tell us how it goes. Thanks to the player who asked for this: *"in app JIT enabling is cool and all, but it doesn't work under LiveContainer"*. Now it should: let us know. Everything else is as in 0.3.2.

With Picture in Picture on, the code still floats over Settings as before; with it off, remember the code before you tap Open Settings. Everything else is as in 0.3.0.

# Playport 0.3.0: 32-bit games **32-bit Windows games now run on your iPhone.** Until now Playport ran only 64-bit games. 0.3.0 adds a full 32-bit runtime with Direct3D 9 graphics on Apple's GPU, and **Portal 2** is the first 32-bit game that plays: menus, test chambers, both portals, sound, controller, saves and Steam Cloud. Everything runs locally on a non-jailbroken iPhone: no streaming, no remake, no PC. ## Highlights ### 🧩 32-bit Windows games - 32-bit (x86) games run next to 64-bit ones, from the same Library and the same Play button. Nothing to set up. - iOS keeps the lowest 4 GB of memory to itself, which is exactly where a 32-bit game has to live. Playport gives each 32-bit game its own 4 GB window higher up and translates every memory access on the fly, so the game never notices. ### 🎨 Direct3D 9 on the iPhone's GPU, through KosmicKrisp - Direct3D 9 runs on DXVK, then Vulkan, then Metal through **KosmicKrisp**, Mesa's Vulkan driver for Apple GPUs, ported to iOS for Playport. - 32-bit games pick Vulkan automatically. Game options show "Default · Vulkan". - KosmicKrisp keeps its compiled shaders on disk, so the second launch of a game reuses them instead of compiling again. ### 🌀 Portal 2 - Plays at **about 60 FPS at 720p**. A 5-minute play with portals, tunnels, a death and a reload averaged 58.4 FPS. - A 95-minute session with saving and loading ran without a crash. After a long session the phone gets warm, and Portal 2 then runs at about 50 FPS. - Saves sync with Steam Cloud, so you can carry on where you left off on your PC. ### ⚡ Faster 32-bit games - x87 floating-point math, which older 32-bit games use heavily, now runs at the CPU's native 64-bit precision, as Valve's Proton does on ARM64. Portal 2's main thread does about 40 % less work and the CPU draws about 40 % less power, so the phone stays cooler and holds 60 FPS for longer. ## Fixes and improvements - Controllers work in games that bring their own copy of XInput (Portal 2 does). - Steam Cloud: Portal 2's saves upload again, and a file Steam refuses no longer stops the whole sync. - Games that ask for Tahoma show their text: Playport now ships fallback Tahoma fonts. - A new opening animation while your stores load, and a launch that dives into the game's art. The game then fades in at its own size. - A game's art fills the screen on its page and during its launch. ## Known limitations - Portal 2 is the only 32-bit game tested so far. Other 32-bit Direct3D 9 games use the same route, but expect rough edges. Please tell us how they run. - 32-bit games run only on Vulkan. Choosing DXMT for one, on its page or globally, stops it from starting. - Expect short hitches when a level loads and the first time you see a new effect. - In long sessions the iPhone heats up and lowers its clock speeds, and frame rates drop. ## Install Download `Playport-0.3.0.ipa` and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version, install over it: your games, saves and Steam login stay. Bring your own games from Steam. # Playport 0.2.0 ## Highlights - Direct3D 12 games run on Vulkan by default. Playport detects a game's Direct3D version and picks the right graphics backend. - You can still choose one yourself in Game options. - New first-run setup that walks you through getting ready to play. - Better Library. Filter by All, Installed or Steam, and tell copies of the same game from different stores apart. ## Fixes and improvements - B takes you back to where you were. - The Home banner opens the game's page. - Long game names fit on the launch screen.

### New - **In-app JIT: no StikDebug needed.** Madeira can enable JIT by itself through a bundled helper built on StikJIT. On iOS 27 it pairs with the iPhone it runs on: in Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, tap **Pair with Madeira** and enter the PIN Madeira shows. No computer needed. On iOS 26, import a pairing file instead. The pairing is kept in the Keychain. StikDebug still works. (#127) - **Play turns JIT on for you.** If JIT is off, Play enables it and then starts the game. The button reads **Starting JIT** meanwhile. - **Madeira JIT shortcut (iOS 27, optional).** LocalDevVPN's loopback does not work over cellular data. The shortcut connects LocalDevVPN, turns Cellular Data off when there is no Wi-Fi, and puts both back once the game has started, along with any VPN you were using. Add it during setup or in Settings › JIT. - **Steam Cloud saves** for installed Steam games, on by default. Saves sync before and after you play, and the cloud copy is backed up before it is replaced. (#130) - **A controller as keyboard and mouse**, chosen per game, with a Controller binds page. DirectInput is now a per-game choice too. (#128) - **Setup** starts by installing LocalDevVPN when it is missing. It opens once more after this update, so you can pick one of the new JIT options. ### Fixed - Games start faster: Wine starts as soon as the wineserver is ready, not after a fixed 2 s. (#125) - Cuphead (#107), Nine Sols (#108) and Hades II (#119, #120) now run, and Steam app info with escaped quotes is read correctly (#118). - JIT errors now explain the problem and offer a fix: **Pair Again** or **Connect LocalDevVPN**. The error also shows on the Settings tab. ### Known issues - With Wi-Fi and Cellular Data both off, LocalDevVPN cannot connect, so JIT cannot be enabled, even with the shortcut. Connect LocalDevVPN while a network is available. ### Install - Requires **iOS 26 or later**. In-app pairing and the Madeira JIT shortcut need iOS 27. - If your sideloader asks whether to keep app extensions, keep them: Madeira's in-app JIT runs in one. - The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device. - First-run setup walks you through JIT. Settings shows JIT and Memory+ with green checks and says **Ready to play**. ### Not included The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see `legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Madeira runs Windows PC games on iPhone in a single app: FEX-Emu translates x86-64 to ARM64, a Wine 11 fork runs as ARM64EC, DXMT maps Direct3D 11 to Metal, and Direct3D 12 runs natively. ### Install - The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. ## MCX360 Edition 1.1 ### New - **On-screen touch controls**, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`. - **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list. - **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen. ### Performance - Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds. - Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60). - The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores. - Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame. ### Fixes - Fixed random crashes after playing for a while. - Fixed choppy audio. - Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing. ### Known issues - Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps. - The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement. Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.

## What's Changed in v1.3.2 🚀 This update brings full feature parity with AirCard macOS v1.2.6, restores robust card discovery across all iOS versions, introduces automatic bank/network recognition with custom card nicknames, delivers an ultra-fast tunnel cache (0.02s connections), and completely resolves wallpaper flashing for Collections and Mercury wallpapers. ### 💳 Wallet Card Discovery & Bank Identification • **Universal Wallet Log Parser**: Ported the proven `WalletScanParser` from AirCard macOS. Captures cards from `Dashboard loading (...): for SOO+`, `passIDs[InSession]`, `passIDs[global]`, and modern JSON NFC activations (`"identifier": "HEX"`). • **Automatic Bank & Network Detection**: Recognizes Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, Discover, and JCB via applet AIDs during selection. • **Card Nicknames (Rename)**: Added a direct **Rename** button (✏️) so you can give your cards friendly names like *"Monobank"*, *"Salary Card"*, or *"Revolut"*, safely persisted in app settings. • **28-Character Fallback Token Matcher**: Restores dependable card discovery on devices where standard log patterns are redacted. ### ⚡ Ultra-Fast Tunnel Routing (from 10s to 0.02s!) • **Working Route Caching**: `rust-core` now caches the active RSD connection route (`LAST_WORKING_ROUTE`), eliminating repeated port and interface scanning. • **RSD-First Priority**: Connects directly via RemoteXPC on port 49152, bypassing slow Lockdown retries and broken pipes on iOS 18+. • **Eliminated Loopback Policy Drops**: Removed local loopback attempts that caused `policy drop` control channel errors. ### 🖼 Wallpapers (.tendies) — Collections & Mercury Fixes • **Dual Injection on iOS 18+**: Wallpapers are now injected into both their primary bundle (`com.apple.WallpaperKit.CollectionsPoster` or `com.apple.MercuryPoster`) and the modern iOS 18+ application container (`com.apple.Posters.CollectionsPosterApp` / `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp`). • **Metadata Synchronization**: Fixed a critical issue where `Wallpaper.plist`'s numeric identifier was randomized out-of-sync with `suggestionMetadata.plist` (`7400.DYNAMIC`), causing wallpapers like Windows 11 to vanish from the Lock Screen gallery. • **Mercury Wallpaper Support**: Added recognition for `mercury-descriptors` container folders and registered `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp` in `PersistedPosterContainerBundleIdentifiers`. • **NeoSpring Respring**: Instant springboard reload to apply wallpaper preferences immediately. ### 🧪 Quality & Testing • All 24 unit tests passing (`TendiesEngineTests`, `WalletScanParserTests`, `CardPhotoCropTests`, `CardPhotoPickerTests`). **Full ## beta 0.2.3 the per-game core settings translated into every language the app speaks, and two texts that were confidently telling people the wrong thing. ### Language - **The per-game core settings are readable in all fourteen languages.** The explanations under LLVM precompilation, SPU block size, resolution scale and the decoder mix existed only in English and Spanish, which meant that everyone else was choosing between values whose consequences were not written down anywhere they could read. Those, the two memory warnings, the settings notebook and the "this device cannot emulate" notice are now translated: 240 strings across the twelve remaining languages. What is still identical to English after this pass is the set of words that are the same word in that language — *Mono*, *Auto*, *Normal*, *Panel*, *Version* in German, *Options* in French — and changing those would only make them worse. ### Text - **The memory warning no longer promises that 8 GB of RAM is enough.** It ended by saying that devices with 8 GB or more need none of this, which is false and was reported by someone holding a phone with 12 GB who had just been blocked by it. The extended virtual addressing entitlement governs address space, not physical memory; extra RAM does not widen it. The notice now says the outcome depends on how the app was installed, which is the part the reader can act on. - **The credits show the version you are actually running.** The version was a translatable string copied by hand into all fourteen language blocks, and it had been left at `beta.0.1` while beta.0.2 was being handed out — three releases

## beta 0.2.0 ### Emulation - **A cache-maintenance call no longer kills the thread that makes it.** `sys_icache_invalidate` touches memory to do its work, so a null pointer takes the caller down with a segfault at address 0. One of the two calls in the SPU recompiler's dispatch path sits on the common exit, where the patch-point pointer is legitimately null because nothing was rewritten. It was killing all five SPURS kernels one after another, which left the game's twelve PPU threads waiting on them forever. From the outside it looked exactly like a hang: no error, CPU at 16 %, millions of idle sleeps. Fixed at the call site, and `psx3ios_jit_flush` now refuses an invalid address and records it instead of dying. - **The graphics layer is back to a state that draws.** A merge from another ARM64 port had left 28 files of the RSX and Vulkan code changed, among them the swapchain, the image-layout transitions and the pipeline compiler. The result was a game that ran perfectly and displayed nothing — broken geometry or a black screen — which is a hard symptom to read, because the emulator looks healthy: it compiles shaders, counts frames and uses CPU. Two additions that had no business in an iOS app went with it: an Android Vulkan loader and a profiler's GPU timer. - **x18 is always reserved on Apple hardware.** It is the platform register and the system may overwrite it at any moment, but LLVM only infers that from the target triple, and ours deliberately says `linux` so that its runtime linker emits ELF and builds the branch islands a 266 MiB code arena needs. It is now reserved in the backend itself, where no chain of options can leave it open, and every launch records whether it took effect. ### Settings - **Your settings now win over the recommended database.** Turning something off for a game was being silently undone at boot: the emulator applies its recommended per-game configuration after everything else, so the database overwrote the user's own choice with no indication anywhere. The recommended values still fill in what you have not touched, but the keys you set for that game are removed from them before they are applied, and the log says how many were dropped. - **The recommended database can be switched off entirely**, and ships off, so a game starts with your settings and nothing else ### Setup - **The guided setup finishes the job.** Everything under Settings → JIT can now be completed without leaving it: enabling JIT, choosing the StikDebug script, and turning on the launch handoff, alongside firmware and the memory entitlements — seven steps instead of five. Each action button shows the real state rather than an instruction, so "JIT enabled" and a script's filename tell you there is nothing left to do on that page. - **Installing firmware no longer closes the setup screen.** It used to dismiss itself so the library could do the work, which dropped the user out halfway through configuration with the distinct impression they had broken something. The file picker is now presented over the guide and the install runs inside it, spinner and all, returning to the same card with the button reading "Firmware installed". ### Interface - **The background colour can be changed**, in Settings → Theme. It tints the gradient, the waves and the specks without touching the theme itself: the two are separate on purpose, since wanting a different colour is not a reason to be given a different layout. Six to choose from, all dark enough to keep what sits on top readable. - **Everything decorative stops while a game runs.** The waves and the specks kept animating behind a game that covered them completely — GPU and battery taken from the emulation to draw something nobody can see. # Iridium 0.2.0 Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**. For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation. Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Check for updates or repair downloaded files while keeping the previous installation. - **Clearer storage warnings.** Download checks use the space available to Iridium and account for verified partial files. **Download Anyway** can bypass an estimated-space warning for one attempt; file verification and real out-of-space errors remain enforced. - **Updated Windows runtime.** Includes 32-bit WoW64 support and D3D9/D3D12 updates. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required. - **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them. ## Known issues - Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading. - Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving. - JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore.
Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.

**Frame rate cap** @Henyckma added an FPS cap that limits presentation only. The game and the audio keep running at full speed, so it costs nothing in emulation and gives back battery and heat instead. Targets are 15, 23.976, 29.94, 30, 45, 59.97, 60, 90 and 120, set globally or per game. The gain is biggest at 2x and 3x internal resolution, where the passes it skips cover the most pixels. Selecting 30 FPS used to halve emulation and audio speed, which is fixed, and FPS profiles from earlier builds carry over without losing the cadence you picked. **Crashes and freezes** Fixed a crash in games like Namco Museum 50th Anniversary, which turned out to be an out of bounds write in the virtual memory page protection table. Fixed a freeze in readback heavy scenes with Hardware Download Mode set to Unsynchronized. Rogue Galaxy no longer stalls the graphics thread around 7.5 ms every frame on a depth probe readback, about a fifth of the frame on an M2. The last two are bmdhacks. Saving per game settings could also leave the game frozen a second or two later, which is covered below. **Sprite hacks** Align Sprite and Merge Sprite apply when you switch them off. This was the third report of that bug and the fifth attempt at it, and the earlier ones all fixed the global screen while leaving everything around it alone. Per game, those rows greyed out whenever GameDB Graphics Fixes was on, kept showing their old value, and got written back on every save. Align Sprite, Merge Sprite and Wild Arms Offset are one Use Global / Off / On picker each now, and they no longer need manual hacks mode. Setting one claims that fix, so the game database stops overriding it while keeping every other fix for the game. Texture Inside RT, Native Scaling, Bilinear Upscale, Unscaled Palette Draw, Preload Frame Data and Disable Partial Invalidation had the same bug and were fixed with it. None of these do anything at 1x internal resolution, which is by design. **Per-game settings** Turning on Use Per-Game Overrides used to soften text and edges: enabling it copied six graphics keys into the per game file, and one of those forced a blend deinterlace that also suppressed the game's own database fix. Only the settings you change are written now. Saving in that panel could also leave the game frozen a second or two later while the emulator carried on at full speed, because metadata scans share one disc image with the running game and a scan during play left it holding a closed disc. The Renderer picker never saved a change made while a game was running, so it never applied either. It saves now, and it moved from Fixes & Compatibility to the Graphics tab where people kept looking for it. It still applies at the next boot of that game. Saving the panel is quicker too: it used to fire one full settings reload per field written, 71 of them for a single Save. **Settings** Every slider, stepper and typed number is one control now, and each setting is described once instead of once per screen. The FPS target had three different sets of bounds across three screens. Sliders stop on values people actually pick, every stop list holds the default so reset lands on one, and typing still reaches anything in between. 2.5.1 is mostly a fixes release. The two biggest issues were A12 devices crashing on launch and rumble being completely broken since 2.4.1. Both are fixed, along with a proper no-JIT fallback, several performance improvements, and a collection of Virtual Pad and interface fixes. ## Highlights * Fixed launch crashes on A12 devices * Controller and phone rumble work again * Added improved phone rumble with separate motor handling and a strength setting — @Henyckma * Added a proper no-JIT fallback and improved interpreter performance — @Henyckma * Fixed a Devil May Cry crash during FMVs * Added fractional Internal Resolution options up to 3.5x * Reduced graphics overhead in several games — @bmdhacks * Improved Rogue Galaxy performance — @bmdhacks * Virtual Pad and layout improvements — @Henyckma * GameDB and cheat-loading fixes — @jpolo1224 ## A12 Devices Fixed launch crashes on iPhone XS, XS Max, XR, iPad Air 3, iPad mini 5, iPad 8 and A12X/A12Z iPad Pro. 2.5.0 was accidentally built with an Apple M1 CPU baseline. iOS now targets `apple-a12`, the oldest device we support. ## Rumble Controller and phone rumble work again after being broken since 2.4.1. @Henyckma also reworked phone rumble. It is now sustained, responds properly to motor strength, handles the two PS2 motors separately, and ramps in and out more naturally. A Phone Rumble Strength setting has been added, and Test Rumble now works without a controller connected. Several controller-rumble bugs were fixed at the same time, including a leak, a threading issue and cases where rumble could be routed to the wrong player. ## Playing Without JIT @Henyckma added a proper fallback for devices where JIT is unavailable. Instead of crashing or showing a black screen, ARMSX2 now falls back to interpreter implementations where possible. Interpreter performance was improved at the same time. On the test device and workload, EE time went from 37.55 ms to 30.55 ms, about 18.6% less. Results vary by game, device and thermal state. ## Crashes and Stability Fixed a Devil May Cry crash when the game switches to the software renderer for FMVs. Several related JIT and software-renderer stability issues were fixed as well, including problems affecting legacy JIT mode under LiveContainer. Fastmem now stays disabled correctly when its required 4 GB virtual mapping cannot be allocated, and a race in the JIT keepalive path was narrowed. ## Graphics and Performance @bmdhacks reduced unnecessary render-pass and copy work. Across a five-loop replay: * Rogue Galaxy: 2,411 → 1,741 render passes * OutRun 2006: 1,240 → 1,118 render passes Vertex processing was also reduced in cases where an auto-flush cannot occur. Dragon Quest VIII measured 4.7% fewer graphics-thread cycles in testing. Internal Resolution now includes: `1.25x`, `1.5x`, `1.75x`, `2.25x`, `2.5x`, `2.75x` and `3.5x` ## Game Database @bmdhacks improved Rogue Galaxy performance by disabling auto-flush for the game. Render passes fall 38% and texture copies 74%, worth about 1.8 ms per frame and 2.6 fps on a low-end device. There is a small visual trade-off: some lamp lighting can appear slightly brighter and warmer than the software renderer reference. Four side-by-side comparisons at 1:1 failed to distinguish the two, but please report it if you notice it during normal play. Need for Speed Underground 1 and 2 now run without hardware readbacks — @jpolo1224. Cheats stored under the generic all-CRC file name work again — @jpolo1224. ## Virtual Pad All of this is @Henyckma's. Dynamic Thumbstick feedback now pulses once when crossing the maximum-pull threshold instead of repeating continuously. Swipe Camera gets the same feedback once it becomes a joystick, and now uses the full left half of the screen on iPad. Saved layouts now have Rename, Share and Delete options. Device Presets no longer change Aspect Ratio or treat it as part of whether a preset is active. ## Interface Fixes * Fixed a crash when toggling Low Power Mode with a video wallpa

ARMSX2 2.5.0 is a major update to the emulator core and the iOS frontend. The biggest core change is a new shared ARM64 recompiler, replacing the older iOS-specific EE, IOP and VU recompilers. It brings iOS in line with the ARM handheld builds, reduces CPU overhead in several parts of emulation, and restores features the previous iOS backend did not support correctly. The release also moves iOS onto the shared game database used by the other mobile ARM builds. That brings a large set of newer per-game fixes and tuning to iOS. Outside the core, 2.5.0 adds Dynamic Controls, animated backgrounds, settings presets, improved frame pacing, proper 120 Hz support, an in-app controller-skin browser, RetroAchievements fixes, OSD improvements, and a long list of graphics and stability fixes. Almost none of this is my own work. The core belongs to @bmdhacks, the new iOS interface and control features to @Henyckma, and the rest to @pstef, @jpolo1224, @XDarkFallenX and Mart. Thanks to all of them, and to everyone who tested development builds and reported problems. ## Highlights * New shared ARM64 recompiler for the EE, IOP and vector units, from @bmdhacks * Updated shared game database with newer fixes and tuning for more than a thousand games * Dynamic Thumbsticks, Swipe Camera, Gyroscope Camera and Dynamic Actions, from @Henyckma * Twelve Metal-rendered Dynamic Background styles, from @Henyckma * Six settings presets plus import and export, from @Henyckma * Emulation-Only Mode, which frees the device to the emulator once a game is running, from @Henyckma * Reworked frame-pacing controls and per-game presets * Proper 120 Hz support on ProMotion devices * Apple GPU fixes for speckled graphics in games such as Black and God of War II, from @bmdhacks * Fixes for upscaling hacks and settings that previously appeared not to apply * In-app controller-skin browser and more reliable skin importing * Working RetroAchievements statistics, achievement lists and native notifications * OSD safe-area, rotation and performance-overlay fixes * Several iOS crashes and core correctness bugs fixed ## New ARM64 Recompiler ARMSX2 now uses the newer shared ARM64 recompiler family written by @bmdhacks and tested primarily on ARM handheld hardware, replacing the older iOS-specific implementations. The new backend has had considerably more testing, including differential tests that compare recompiled EE, IOP and VU execution against other emulator implementations. It also contains substantial optimization work around register handling, larger compiled blocks, vector instructions, calls and returns, unaligned memory accesses, and self-modifying code. Several features that were missing from the previous iOS backend are also supported now: * Dynamic game patches can be applied from the game database. Entries such as the ones used by Armored Core: Nine Breaker and Ratchet & Clank 2 previously had no effect on iOS. * Goemon's TLB handling now has the required preload and invalidation hooks. The fix remains behind the existing game fix and would still benefit from a complete playthrough test. * Delay-slot swapping is supported where the PS2 allows it. The JIT has also been adapted to the different executable-memory paths used by the app, including the iOS 26 TXM paths, Simulator support, and the legacy path used on iOS 18 and earlier. ## Game Compatibility iOS no longer ships its own separate merged game database. ARMSX2 now uses the shared database. The move onto the shared resources was done by @bmdhacks. The previous iOS copy had fallen behind upstream. With the shared database, more than a thousand games have different behavioral entries compared with 2.4.1, and future mobile fixes no longer need to be copied separately into the iOS version. Some of the more visible changes include: * Hardware-readback tuning is now actually applied from the game database, thanks to @jpolo1224 making the database key work at all. Forty-eight games currently use it, including Black,

ARMSX2 2.6.2 Emulation Fixes: ESPN NFL 2K5 no longer freezes during early gameplay and now works as intended. Ratchet & Clank: Deadlocked, restored two COP2/VU0 sync fixes lost in the monorepo migration, plus a monotonic-clock guard that stopped the EE being slammed backwards. Game is now playable, although one graphical issue remains from my testing. Folder memory cards work on a custom data folder again. Creating save data crashed or reported "format failed" for anyone whose data folder wasn't internal app storage. Texture Packs: Importing a pack no longer freezes the app when using an SD card. A real pack is thousands of files over SAF, and the copy ran on the UI thread, black screen, then "ARMSX2 isn't responding", worse on SD. Import and delete now run in the background with a live file count to let you know when it's completed. BC/DXT packs work on GPUs without hardware support. Devices that don't expose textureCompressionBC, Adreno 650-class hardware, and Mesa Turnip on any Adreno, silently dropped every texture in a pack. Those are now decoded on the CPU. Texture Packs are now reachable in-game, from the pause menu, with a Restart Game to Apply button. Packs are only loaded at boot. The Texture Manager now shows which folder the emulator will actually read, and warns when no installed pack matches it. Booting a raw .ELF derives the folder name from the filename rather than the disc serial, which silently sent packs to a folder nothing scanned. Memory card import now accepts folders instead of just zips of folders. Folder cards are directories, but the picker only accepted files, so a zipped card was renamed to .ps2 and read as unformatted. Folder cards can now be imported unpacked from a zip, with validation and a clear error instead of a bad card. Settings & Behaviour: Made more improvements to per-game settings, now apply when launching from a frontend (Cocoon, Daijisho, ES-DE). External launches passed no game identity, so every title fell back to global settings, including per-game memory cards and orientation. (please report if this still misbehaves.) Patches work with RetroAchievements Hardcore enabled again. Hardcore blocked all on-disk patch files in the new UI, while the bundled ones stayed active, so the same widescreen or bug-fix patch worked from our archive and silently died from disk. Cheats remain blocked. Overscan Crop (Settings --> Fixes), trim pixels from any edge to hide garbage or black bars games leave in the area a CRT would have cut off. Measured in native pixels, so it behaves the same at any resolution. Custom OSD colours, including from the in-game menu. Support for Custom game names in the Info tab. GameDB, merged community PRs from @XDarkFallenX Rendering/perf fixes: Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 1 & 2, Everybody's Golf 4, Magna Carta: Tears of Blood, Rumble Racing, Atelier Iris 2 & 3, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance 1 & 2, Jak 3, Kingdom Hearts II, Downhill Domination, Driv3r, Black, God Hand, Musashi: Samurai Legend, Aeon Flux, Artonelico: Melody of Elemia

ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.1 is a much bigger follow-up than the version number might suggest. This update adds video library backgrounds, MetalFX upscaling, more flexible controller and RetroAchievements settings, save-state previews, and a long list of interface improvements. There has also been a lot of work under the hood. JIT handling is more resilient, several ARM64 and Metal paths have been improved, and a number of game-specific compatibility problems have been fixed. Thank you to everyone who tested the builds, reported issues, and kept checking the fixes. ## Library backgrounds Library backgrounds have been rebuilt around separate portrait and landscape slots. Setting a portrait background no longer replaces the landscape one, or vice versa. Each slot clearly shows its orientation, file type, and size, so it is easier to see exactly what you are editing. Each orientation also has its own fit mode: * **Fill** fills the screen and crops the edges when necessary. * **Fit** keeps the entire image visible and may add letterboxing. * **Stretch** fills the screen by changing the image proportions. Stretch mode has been fixed so it no longer leaves black bars along the sides in portrait or at the top and bottom in landscape. Alongside static and animated images, the library can now use looping video backgrounds. MP4, MKV, and WebM files can be selected, and the player swaps cleanly when a different video is chosen. Videos resume properly after returning to the app and pause while ARMSX2 is in the background. Background importing is also safer. A failed import can no longer remove or replace the background you were already using. The dimming control now shows a live percentage, making it easier to use the same intensity across different backgrounds. ## Game cards Portrait game cards finally receive the same frosted-glass treatment as their landscape versions. A subtle gradient behind the cards gives the glass something consistent to blur, while Reduce Transparency users receive an opaque fallback. The cards themselves have received a small layout pass: * Titles, file information, size, and region are centered beneath the cover. * Additional padding gives the contents more breathing room. * The favorite star has a lighter and less distracting background. * The BIOS Only button is easier to notice. * Favorite buttons in the list view have a larger and more reliable tap area. ## Save states and memory cards Save states now display the screenshot captured with each state. This should make it much easier to recognise the point in the game you are about to restore. Memory cards can be exported through the standard iOS share sheet. ZIP archives containing memory cards can also be imported directly into the app. ## Gameplay and controls Portrait gameplay uses more of the available screen. The game viewport has been increased from 55% to 60% of the screen height, reducing the unused space between the game and the virtual controller. The in-game pause button now uses a proper pause symbol instead of the previous ellipsis icon. The menu button also has better contrast, helping it remain visible over bright game scenes. ARMSX2 now keeps the display awake while a game is running. ### Stick inversion Each virtual stick axis can be inverted independently: * Left stick horizontal * Left stick vertical * Right stick horizontal * Right stick vertical These options have global defaults and can also be overridden for individual games. The on-screen stick still follows your finger normally; only the input sent to the game is inverted. ### Rumble and haptics When no rumble-capable physical controller is connected, PS2 rumble events can now be translated into iPhone haptic feedback. This respects the existing Haptic Feedback setting and is rate-limited so sustained rumble does not overload the device’s haptic engine. ## Pause menu Long game titles use end truncation instead of cutting text out of the middle, which keeps the beginning of the title readable. The

ARMSX2 2.6.0.5 What's new: Gyro + stick now work together. Aim gyro (and steering gyro) is now added on top of the physical stick instead of fighting it, use the right stick for coarse aim and tilt to fine-tune, both at once. The other stick (movement) is unaffected while you aim. Fixed: per-game stick fixes leaked to every game. Right/Left Stick Invert X/Y, Swap X/Y, and D-pad as Left Stick now save per game when set in a game's properties (they were writing the global setting for all games). Added Per-game BIOS option. Long-press a game --> Per-game BIOS button to boot that specific game with its own BIOS (like for a EU disc on a EU BIOS, a US disc on a US BIOS). Global BIOS is the default you choose, "Use global" reverts it. Online patches now work from the library. The patch/cheat browser reads the game's serial straight from the disc, so you can browse and install patches from a game's per-game settings without booting it first (previously it only worked in-game). ANGLE is now an OpenGL driver option. When you select the OpenGL renderer, the driver picker shows an ANGLE option (GLES-on-Vulkan), the OpenGL counterpart to the Vulkan driver list. Helps non-Adreno GPUs (Mali/Xclipse/PowerVR) whose native OpenGL driver is weak. Available in both the Renderer settings and the in-game Graphics menu. New GPU driver source: ExynosTools (WearyConcern1165/ExynosTools) added to the in-app driver downloader, helps Xclipse devices on Vulkan.

ARMSX2 2.6.0.4 What's new: Fast-Forward button in the in-game menu, the Session tab now has a one-tap Fast-Forward (between Continue and Restart). It kicks the game to max speed and resumes, reopen the menu and it shows an "On" state to switch it back off. (Same as the Frame limit button, but more obvious). GPU driver recommendation, added back the feature from the old UI, the driver picker now shows your detected GPU model and the recommended driver source for it. Appears in both the in-game menu's driver section and full Settings. For Gyro, pick the aim stick option, Aim mode can now drive the Right or Left analog stick (per-game), for games that aim with the left stick such as Resident Evil 4. Fixes: Cheats/patches on-off toggle now works on PNACH files saved with (CRLF) line endings, no more "Couldn't update … (unusual formatting)" popup. Fixes to the Online browser manager as well. More GameDB game fixes now baked in, thanks to @XDarkFallenX and tester Jer for helping with these! MotoGP 3: Minimum Blending Level 0, fixes transparency effects Evil Dead: A Fistful of Boomstick, Minimum Blending Level 0, fixes transparency effects Resident Evil: Outbreak, Minimum Blending Level 0, fixes transparency effects Marvel: Ultimate Alliance, Instant VU1 off + MTVU off, fixes broken rendering SBK 09: Superbike World Championship, MTVU off, fixes broken rendering Cy Girls (Ice & Aska discs), Round Sprite 2, fixes NPCs walking on-screen Plus upstream GS texture-cache improvements (better clears, format-overlap handling, preload). Enjoy!

ARMSX2 Refresh 2.6.0.3 What's new: Custom achievement unlock sounds: pick any audio file (like the Xbox 360 achievement sound) for RetroAchievements unlocks, in the RetroAchievements --> options screen. Hide games from your library: long-press a game --> Hide from library, with a Show hidden games toggle to bring them back and un-hide in the dropdown toolbar in the top right. Clear cached data in Settings --> App: frees space by wiping the shader and cover-art caches (they rebuild automatically). Green Play button in a game's per-game settings to launch it directly. Optional game titles under cover art now work in the Shelf library layout as well. Fixes: Per-game settings no longer stick to the last game after closing it, and now open correctly from the Shelf layout. Fixed the ANGLE renderer crashing / black-screening on Mali-G77 devices (Retroid Pocket 4 Pro, etc.). This mode is recommended for many Mali users, and may help other kinds of devices as well. Major Vulkan speedup on Mali GPUs, brought back accurate blending now runs in-tile instead of the slow per-primitive barrier fallback (re-enabled the fast feedback-loop path modern Mali drivers support, was present in V38 but was lost in the unification). The in-game Performance tab is now a yellow ⚡.
